reason: I need local material for paving, so digging the workshop ground seems like a natural first step.
expectation: I expect to collect loose soil or regolith for processing.

alternatives.reason: The mesh and stock might make a useful frame, but I want material to pave with first.

effect: The excavation supplied regolith as expected; I need to prepare it for paving.
reaction: A straightforward start; I am curious how the loose material becomes solid.
reason: This is the only available combination and may make a screen or frame for processing the regolith.
expectation: I expect a mesh mounted in an aluminium frame, though its exact use is uncertain.

effect: The frame is a sieve, so I can sort the excavated material.
reaction: The repurposed cargo mesh makes physical sense and is satisfying.
reason: Sieving the regolith should separate coarser pieces; it is also the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect a more uniform fraction of regolith suitable for processing.

effect: The graded regolith is ready for the furnace, suggesting heat will bind it.
reaction: The progression is clear, although the grading result gives little detail.
reason: The furnace is the sole offered next action and heat may fuse the grains into paving.
expectation: I expect heated or sintered regolith, possibly a paving slab.

effect: Heating produced blocks after a slower cycle and revealed the goal of laying them on the workshop ground.
reaction: I like the concrete detail of a failed edge and the limited structural purpose; it makes the process feel less magical.
reason: Laying the blocks on the ground directly serves the new floor goal and is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect a paved workshop floor with less loose dust.

effect: Laying the blocks completed the floor and the chapter as expected.
reaction: It is satisfying to finish the practical improvement, though the final result is terse.

mostWorthwhile.text: The furnace passage was most worthwhile: the flaking first trial, slower cycle and limited purpose give the material a believable practical context.

leastWorthwhile.text: The graded regolith result was terse; I wanted to know what the sieve removed and why the grading matters.

surprise.text: The first firing flaked and a slower cycle produced sound blocks; that small failure made the manufacturing process more interesting.

arbitrary.text: No action felt arbitrary, though after the initial choice the single available combinations made the sequence feel more like following instructions than making decisions.

continue.text: Yes, I would try another chapter to see more practical uses of local materials and scientific discoveries, although I hope for more meaningful choices.
